Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
847 PM PST Sun Nov 22 2026

.SYNOPSIS...22/437 PM.

There will be a chance of light rain through tonight as a weak
cold front moves over the area. Warm and dry conditions are
expected Monday into Tuesday. Light rain is possible again 
Tuesday night into Wednesday, mainly north of Point Conception. 
Thanksgiving will be dry and warmer.

&&

.SHORT TERM (SUN-WED)...22/846 PM.

***UPDATE***

Clouds increased over the area today as the front moved through,
bringing showers and isolated thunderstorms to the region. The
coastal waters and areas along the Central Coast saw the most 
rainfall so far, with quite a few locations seeing totals from
0.25 to 0.40 inches. Totals were much lower further inland,
ranging from 0.15 to 0.05 inches. Still seeing plenty of shower
activity tonight from the Channel Islands to the Ventura/Santa 
Barbara County line to along the LA County coasts, and these
showers will move east, and die off overnight. There is still a 
small chance for isolated heavier showers at times, mostly 
favoring the coasts.

Low clouds and fog are expected to develop over the northern
interior areas, which should limit cooling in those areas.
However, the Antelope Valley along with some foothills locations
should see overnight low temperatures fall to near freezing
temperatures. Therefore, frost advisories were issued for tonight
into tomorrow morning for the Antelope Valley and the eastern
Antelope Valley foothills. Other interior areas may have spots
that fall close to freezing temperatures, but clouds should
inhibit cooling in these regions. 

Following the front, brief ridging builds in Monday and Tuesday,
and developing offshore winds will start off a warming trend that
should last through the week. High temperatures should reach the 
upper 60s to 70s many areas Wednesday. However, light showers are
possible for northern San Luis Obispo County as early as Tuesday 
night, becoming more convective Wednesday. Again, most of the more
intense showers should be over the waters and at the coasts. 

***From Previous Discussion***

Overall, latest model guidance indicates no major changes to
previous forecast thinking for the short term period. 

Through tonight, a weak cold front will sweep across the area.
Currently, the front is impacting San Luis Obispo and Santa
Barbara counties with some light shower activity. As the front 
moves south and east, Ventura and Los Angeles counties will have
the threat of showers late this evening and overnight. Rainfall
totals, if any, will be rather light with amounts around 0.25 
inches or less expected (with the highest totals likely across 
Santa Barbara county). No significant hydrologic issues are 
expected.

For Monday and Tuesday, an upper level ridge will pop up over the
area, peaking in strength on Monday. At the same time, weak
offshore pressure gradients will develop, peaking in strength on
Tuesday morning. So, warm and dry conditions can be expected
across the area. High temperatures will peak on Tuesday with
widespread upper 60s to mid 70s across the coasts and coastal
valleys. As for winds, there will be some northeasterly winds due
to the offshore pressure gradients. However with minimal upper
level support, the offshore winds will remain weak and well below
advisory levels. 

For Tuesday night and Wednesday, another weak system will impact
the area. Based on latest guidance, this particular system will
only bring a grazing shot of rain to San Luis Obispo and Santa
Barbara counties Tuesday night and Wednesday morning with rain
totals of 0.25 inches or less. For Ventura and Los Angeles
counties, the chances for any measurable rain are less than 15%
Tuesday night and Wednesday. As for temperatures, there will
actually be a bit of warming for most areas on Wednesday as an
upper level ridges noses in behind the weak front.

.LONG TERM (THU-SUN)...22/123 PM.

For the extended period, no major changes to previous forecast
thinking.

For Thanksgiving Day and Black Friday, the combination of a strong
upper level ridge (588-590 DM heights) and weak offshore surface
pressure gradients will bring warm and dry conditions to the area.
High temperatures will peak on Friday with coastal and coastal
valley areas topping out in the 70s to lower 80s while interior
sections climb into the mid 60s to lower 70s. Essentially, most
areas will be about 4-8 degrees above seasonal normals. As for
winds, there will be some northeasterly winds across the area.
However with limited upper level support, the northeast winds are
expected to remain weak and the chances for advisory-level winds
is very low. 

For Saturday and Sunday, another weak system will move across the
area. Models differ in the timing of this system, but agree on the
fact it will not be very impressive. Current rainfall estimates
for this system are generally for under 0.25 inches for the area.
However northwest San Luis Obispo county (Rocky Butte area) could
get up to 0.75 inches of rain. With the passing systems,
temperatures will tumble back down into the 60s to around 70.

&&

.AVIATION...23/0041Z.

At 0023Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer and no inversion.

Moderate confidence in the 00Z TAFs through 15Z Monday. There is
a 20-40 percent chance of -shra for the coastal and valley TAF
sites, but the timing of rain may differ by +/- 2 hours from TAF 
times.
KLAX...Moderate to high confidence in the 00Z TAF. High
confidence in VFR conds but moderate confidence in the timing of 
any -SHRA. Light northeast winds are possible from 12Z to 16Z. Any
east wind component is expected to be 7 kt or less thru the fcst 
period. 

KBUR...Moderate to high confidence in the 00Z TAF. High
confidence in VFR conds but moderate confidence in the timing of 
any -SHRA.

&&

.MARINE...22/724 PM.

High confidence that winds and seas will remain below small craft
advisory (SCA) levels through Tuesday night.

Two storms are expected to affect the area. The first is crossing
the waters this evening and will move clear of the area later
tonight. Another storm will move over the area Tuesday night
through Wednesday. The second systems will bring the best chance 
of rain to the seas north of Pt Conception. Post- frontal low-end 
SCA level NW-W winds will be possible Wednesday/night south of 
Point Conception. A significant westerly swell (around 14-16 feet)
is expected mid- week, with large, SCA level seas for the outer 
waters.

&&

.BEACHES...22/746 PM.

There is significant concern for moderate to major coastal 
flooding Thanksgiving week. This is due to the combination of 
kelvin wave/thermal expansion, Perigean spring tides, and a large
long-period westerly swell (260-280 degrees).

===============================================================

[For Central Coast, Ventura, and Los Angeles counties]:

A COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY is in effect for Monday- Tuesday.

Potential impacts: shallow flooding of beach parking lots and 
unprotected roads, moderate beach erosion likely, isolated damage 
to structures/building/roadways but could occur but is unlikely. 

A COASTAL FLOOD WATCH is in effect for WEDNESDAY- THURSDAY.

The swell will arrive during this period which will combine with 
the aforementioned factors. Still some uncertainty in regards to 
how timely these will combine, but regardless significant impacts 
seem probable. Timing of peak high tides are expected between 845 
AM-1000 AM and predicted values are: roughly 8.2-8.4 ft for 
LA/VTA and 7.9-8.2 ft for Central Coast. The reasonable worst case
scenario is 0.3-0.5 ft above these values. A slight limiting 
factor that may prevent the worst case scenario from materializes 
would be higher mean sea level pressure.

Potential impacts if upgraded to COASTAL FLOOD WARNING:

More extensive moderate coastal flooding reaching further inland,
moderate to high risk of damaging flooding of coastal roads and 
structures, and significant beach erosion is likely.

Areas of greatest concern: Morro Bay, Pismo Beach, Oceano Dunes, 
& Cayucos/Avila/Pismo Piers. For LA: Santa Monica to Palo Verdes 
and Long Beach/Naples. For VTA, Faria to Silver Strand Beach 
including inside of harbors and Ventura Harbor.

A HIGH SURF ADVISORY has been issued for the Central Coast from 
Sunday morning through Thursday afternoon.

Surf of up to 11 feet expected Monday morning with a lull in high
surf Monday night into Tuesday followed by rapid building to 
10-15 feet Wednesday morning and to 15 to 22 feet Wednesday 
afternoon and evening. There is an increasing likelihood the High
Surf Advisory will need to eventually be upgraded to a High Surf 
Warning probably by Tuesday. There is also a risk of breaking
waves in the Morro Bay Entrance early Wednesday through Wednesday
night and possibly into Thursday. 

For the Ventura and Los Angeles County beaches, elevated to high 
surf is expected for much of the upcoming week, peaking Wednesday 
and Thursday with likely High Surf Advisories. There is even the 
small chance of Warning-level surf up to 15 feet for the Ventura 
County coast during this period and a risk of breaking waves in
the Ventura Harbor Entrance early Wednesday through Wednesday
night. 

==================================================================

[For Santa Barbara South Coast & Catalina/Santa Barbara islands]:

A COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY has been issued for Monday-Thursday.

Potential impacts: shallow flooding of beach parking lots and 
unprotected roads, moderate beach erosion likely, isolated
damage to structures/building/roadways but could occur but is
unlikely. 

Areas of greatest concern: Santa Barbara to Rincon and Jalama
Beach. 

Additional Information: Elevated to high surf is likely through
Thanksgiving week. Additional coastal hazards will likely be
needed for Friday.

==================================================================

In conclusion, this is a particularly concerning period for 
coastal flooding risks and high surf - Please read the "actions" 
section below. 

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS:

(1)Heed advice from local officials - Rely on their expertise
regarding preparedness, closures, and warnings. 

(2)Protect property - Take necessary actions such as setting up
sandbags or barriers in flood-prone areas.

(3)Avoid flood areas - Stay clear of rock jetties, and flooded
roads, walkways, and other normally dry places.

(4)Stay off the beach - large breaking waves can cause injury, 
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near 
shore.

(4)Monitor the forecast for latest information: weather.gov/LOX
and @nwslosangeles on social media. Be aware of when high tide
peaks in your area: tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov. Refer to LAXCFWLOX.
